text:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH mem on hosted-gpu-pool-7 — KV-cache growth detected, sustained for ~18m. Error spike -> 503s; routing affected. Paging oncall: @sam. Alert: <https://alerts.internal/r/hosted-gpu-7> :rotating_light:

sam: I'm on it, joining. quick summary of impact?

nina: support seeing several customer tickets: ticket#54321 reports truncated responses + 500/503s, started ~20m ago. ~7 customers with >5% error uplift.

tasha: looking at runtime metrics — continuous-batching window for some sessions exploded (per-session token window ~400k-750k). KV map entries for those sessions grew without bound due to a malformed system prompt loop from a single customer cohort (chat-prod-uk). Logs show repeated append_context loops for session_id=sess-9f3a.

m_weiss: did we roll any batch-related configs earlier today? I pushed a batch-window tuning change to hosted pools this morning (increase max_batch_size from 64 -> 256) to improve throughput.

sam: that matches the timing. rolling back batch-config to previous commit now and disabling aggressive prefetch on the hosted pool.

tasha: executing mitigation steps now:
```
# disable prefetch on pool
kubectl set env ds/kv-prefetch PREFETCH_ENABLED=false -n hosted-runtime
# rollback batch config
kubectl rollout undo ds/batching-config -n hosted-runtime
```

leo: ops hat: enabling eviction hook on affected nodes to reclaim KV memory and break runaway sessions. running: /ops/enable-evict.sh --pool hosted-gpu-pool-7 :wrench:

sam: applying temporary per-session cap (global override) to stop new sessions growing KV unbounded:
```
curl -X POST https://config.internal/patch -d '{"max_session_kv":"1024"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```

tasha: after rollback + prefetch off + eviction, mem usage on 2/3 impacted nodes dropped ~65% in 5m. one node still GC'ing, seeing repeated kv_alloc OOM logs.

leo: scaled down continuous-batcher replicas on that pool as a stopgap to reduce concurrent KV growth.

nina: customer comms: sent initial note to affected customers — short update + ETA. prepping follow-up once we confirm stability.

amy: recommended message approved: "we experienced memory-pressure causing degraded responses for a subset of customers. engineering applied mitigations; we're monitoring recovery and expect full restoration within 45 minutes."

sam: monitoring. creating incident channel #incident-kv-session-swell and adding SRE + runtime + support. will hand off to morning shift at 07:00 UTC unless escalation required.

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity -> Sev2. Pager cleared for current oncall. Please update incident channel with postmortem timeline and customer impact numbers. :white_check_mark:
